deposits.notes: The only data/code repository URL printed in the paper (PDF p. 10, line 329); the form's data_url and code_url repeat it. Its web page returned HTTP 200 but only the generic OSF application shell. Unauthenticated requests to https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/eapdn/, https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/eapdn/files/osfstorage/, and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/eapdn/children/ each returned HTTP 401 with detail: Authentication credentials were not provided. Stopped without logging in or requesting access. This confirms an authentication/authorization barrier, not that creating an account would grant access. The paper describes de-identified processed GROUP-level data and analysis code here; actual files, license, rows, columns and variables could not be verified, so they remain unknown rather than being inferred from manuscript tables. The paper separately states that raw proposals, chat logs, LLM records, activity logs, personal drafts and individual survey responses are available on request under an IRB-compliant data-use agreement with redaction. S1 coverage is attributed from that statement, not verified from files.

The paper cites AsPredicted #275284 in PDF p. 21, S1.1; the exact public URL was supplied by the PsyArXiv preprint API's prereg_links field. The URL returned HTTP 200 with an HTML rendering, and its ordinary Download PDF link returned HTTP 200 and a 201166-byte, two-page PDF, read in memory. Title: Human-AI Collaboration on Group Creativity- Hangzhou, China, 2026 (#275284). Preregistered 2026/02/24 05:04 (PT). The record is public while its four authors are anonymous for peer review; no login was required. It contains hypotheses, proposed measures, the five planned conditions, exclusion rules and a planned sample of 450 participants in 150 three-person groups. It contains no observations, actual allocation records, outcome scores or participant-generated ideas. Its planned sample does not establish the actual randomized counts. No study-specific data/code deposit link was present. The earlier identifier-based request https://aspredicted.org/blind.php?x=275284 returned HTTP 200 but only a generic page; the exact preprint-provided URL resolved the record. No explicit reusable-data license was confirmed.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 with unauthenticated Python urllib requests and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. Read the complete 161226-character markdown conversion, including all appendices, and verified quoted passages against the 70-page saved PDF using PyMuPDF. Quotes preserve wording and punctuation with line wraps, marginal line/page numbers, font ligatures and the wrapped word Information normalized. The PDF has only one external URI annotation, https://osf.io/eapdn; that URL and both identical URLs in the form's data_and_code were checked. No other data/code/materials repository link was found in the paper. The single randomized study in the form is S1, with team assignment and team-level creative outputs; manuscript inventories reporting 444 people and 148 teams are not file inspections and are not recorded as rows_checked. Status is on_request because the paper explicitly makes the raw participant information and texts available only on request under a data-use agreement. The claimed processed-data/code project additionally has an observed HTTP 401 access barrier. The three deposits/resources above comprise that project, the public preregistration and the public manuscript; the latter two are not participant datasets. No public analyzable participant, output-with-participant-ID or team-level dataset was confirmed by reading columns. Searches by the main title, supplementary title and first author across DataCite, Zenodo, Harvard Dataverse and OSF found no alternative relevant data deposit. Therefore none of the missing statistics in final.open_items can currently be computed from verified public data: in particular, Supplementary Table 15's dispersion type for S1-O7/S1-O8/S1-O10 cannot be checked against the inaccessible generating code or processed records, and actual initial randomized counts cannot be recovered from planned preregistration counts. Additional participant-level arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts and text-based diversity measures also cannot be recomputed. Rater identities/subset membership remain unverified; the character-count measure code is an Atlas vocabulary issue. Separately, the online PDF hash match establishes that the saved manuscript is the currently listed PsyArXiv v1, addressing part of the version-provenance open item without yielding any new outcome statistic. No credentials were used, no access request was made, and downloaded documents were held only in memory.
